newsitem.title: UK: UK unions against nationalisation, except rail.
newsitem.headline: UK unions against nationalisation, except rail.

text.p: BLACKPOOL, England, Sept 13 (Friday) - Britain's trade unions called on Friday for a future Labour government to bring the railway industry back into public ownership, but they rejected the renationalisation of all privatised industries.

The annual conference of the Trades Union Congress (TUC) backed a motion calling for "the complete renationalisation of the whole railway industry, as a reintegrated national network, and to start the extension of public ownership to the whole railway industry with the acquisition of the TOCs and Railtrack early within its first term of office".
The TOCs are the various train-operating companies that run services around the country. Railtrack owns the infrastructure, including the track and stations.
TUC general secretary John Monks told delegates he was proud to support that motion, but he dismissed a call for blanket renationalisation as "dogmatic".

The National Union of Mineworkers had asked delegates to call upon a Labour government to take back into public ownership "all industries and services, including mining, rail, electricity, gas and water" privatised since 1979 by the Conservative government.
It wanted this done within the first term of a Labour government. A government is elected for five years, but can call an election earlier.
"Rather simplistic calls for wholesale nationalisation have been rejected by this conference since 1988. They deserve to be rejected now," Monks said.
The NUM motion was overwhelmingly defeated.
